entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please wait while we connect you to the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is David. How can I help you today?
Yeah, David, this VeloBand you sold me is a piece of junk. It's completely broken and I want my money back. Now.
I'm certainly sorry to hear that you're having trouble with your device. To make sure I understand, what specifically is the issue? Is it a technical fault or a preference issue?

Are you serious? It's a technical fault! This thing is defective! It's not working at all. It won't sync with my phone, the data is garbage. I'm not paying for broken equipment. I want a refund and I want it now, or I'm lighting you up on every review site on the internet.
Okay, I understand your frustration, and I apologize for the inconvenience. Let me see what I can do. To pull up your order, can I get your email address?
It's sam.jones@email.com. And you better handle this, or I want to speak to your manager immediately.
Thank you, Sam. One moment while I pull that up... Okay, I see your order for the VeloBand Cadence Sensor, delivered 14 days ago. Let me just check the return policy for you.
There's nothing to check. It's broken. Give me my money back.
Yes, I see that right here. According to our policy, you are well within the 90-day window for a return. I can absolutely process that for you.
Oh. Well, good. That's what I thought. So you're sending me a label?

That's correct. I have just authorized the return. A pre-paid shipping label is on its way to your email right now. Simply pack the defective sensor back in the box, apply the label, and drop it off. As soon as our warehouse receives it, a full refund will be issued to your original form of payment.
Okay. That's what should have happened in the first place. Thank you.
You are very welcome. I'm glad I could resolve this for you. Is there anything else I can help with today?
Great. Thank you for calling VeloFit, and have a better day.
